issues.overall_effect: The claimed exact relation between the feature kernel and the GP covariance kernel in the related-work comparison is incorrect. This does not feed the main PDE theorems, but it makes that supporting calculation unreliable.
issues.title: Incorrect Gaussian convolution in GP comparison

diagnostic_evidence.quote: (u,g) &\mapsto B(x, u, g) &&\text{is continuous for almost all } x \in \partial D,
x &\mapsto B(x, u, g) &&\text{is bounded and $\nu_{\partial D}$-measurable for all } (u,g) \in \R\times \R^{d}.

issues.failure_explanation: The Caratheodory hypothesis only gives continuity in the state variables for almost every spatial point, and the almost-everywhere qualifier is not tied to the loss measures \nu_D and \nu_{\partial D}. Pointwise convergence of u and its derivatives therefore does not imply convergence of E[u] or B[u] at every x, as claimed in the lemma.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the lemma's conclusion to convergence for \nu_D-a.e. x in D and \nu_{\partial D}-a.e. x in \partial D, and add that E and B are continuous in the state variables at those measure-a.e. points (or strengthen the Caratheodory assumption accordingly).
issues.overall_effect: The lemma as stated is false in general. Proofs of existence and convergence that invoke it need convergence only for the relevant measure-a.e. points, so the statement and its use must be repaired by adding the appropriate a.e. hypothesis or weakening the conclusion.
issues.title: Lemma continuity asserts pointwise convergence for all x under only a.e. Caratheodory continuity
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local change of quantifier and a standard measure-a.e. hypothesis. It does not alter the method, rates, or main architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: x &\mapsto E(x, u, g, H) &&\text{is bounded and $\nu_D$-measurable for all } (u,g,H) \in \R\times \R^{d} \times \R^{d^2},

issues.failure_explanation: The proof assumes that L(u_mu) is finite and lower semicontinuous along bounded measures, but Caratheodory boundedness in x for fixed state variables does not give uniform boundedness or a growth condition on E and B over the C^2 sublevel sets used by the minimizing sequence. Without such a condition, the loss need not be well-defined or lower semicontinuous.

failure_location.quote: The sparse minimization problem \eqref{eq:sparse_min} admits at least one global minimizer.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a standard growth or uniform boundedness assumption for E and B on the relevant C^2 sublevel sets, or assume directly that the loss is proper and weak-* lower semicontinuous on the sublevel sets.
issues.overall_effect: The existence of minimizers for the continuous and empirical RKBS problems is not established under the stated assumptions. Downstream convergence and representer results that start from global minimizers inherit this gap.
issues.title: Existence theorem lacks growth/properness assumptions for the loss
issues.why_classification: This is more than a typo: a substantive hypothesis is missing for a main theorem. The repair is contained and standard, but it changes the stated assumptions supporting the result.

The source only gives a vague appeal to classical approximation theory with an undefined constant C(K, ||e||) and no proof that the discrete measures converge uniformly on such infinite-dimensional sets. Setwise measure convergence alone does not imply the required uniform equivalence.

The prose justification for density invokes universal approximation in C^0, which does not establish density in the Sobolev/regularity space \U_o. Thus the proof step 'by density of \cV in \U_o' is unsupported for the RKBS actually used in the theorem and algorithm.

issues.failure_explanation: The representer argument reduces to the convex problem minimizing the total variation norm subject to the fixed linear constraint l[u_mu] = \vec l. The relevant ball radius is the optimal value of that norm problem (equivalently the norm of a minimizer for that fixed l), not the optimal value of the original nonlinear regularized empirical problem. As written, the ball B_{t^*} need not contain the constrained minimizer, so the cited extreme-point representation is not justified.

failure_location.quote: where \( t^\ast \) is the optimal value of \eqref{eq:empirical_sparse_min}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define t^* as the optimal value of the constrained norm-minimization problem (or use \|\bar\mu\|_{M(\Omega)}) and adjust the proof accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the finite representer theorem is invalid as written, although the theorem may be repairable by correcting the definition of t^*.
issues.title: Representer proof uses the wrong optimal value for the norm ball
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local fix to a scalar in the proof and does not change the theorem's conclusion or the overall method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let \(\hat{\omega}\) be a coefficient with \(\abs{p[u](\hat{\omega})} > \alpha\). Then, the Dirac delta function at \(\hat{\omega}\) with negative sign of \(p[u](\hat{\omega})\) associated solution perturbation
is a descent direction for~\eqref{eq:finite_min_compact} at \(u = \cN \mu\).

issues.failure_explanation: The formula uses -sgn(|p[u](\hat\omega)|), which equals -1 whenever |p|>0. The descent direction should be -sgn(p[u](\hat\omega)) times the feature, because the loss directional derivative is linear in the coefficient. As written, when p[u](\hat\omega)<0 the proposed direction increases the loss and is not a descent direction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \sgn(\abs{p[u](\hat\omega)}) by \sgn(p[u](\hat\omega)) in the definition of the perturbation.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical justification for the greedy insertion direction is false as stated. The algorithm itself only uses |p| and initializes new coefficients to zero, so the practical scheme is not directly broken, but the formal proposition is.
issues.title: Boosting descent direction uses sign of absolute value
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol correction restores the intended descent statement without changing the algorithm or main results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We use an empty network as the initialization of Algorithm \ref{alg:main} unless otherwise specified.

issues.failure_explanation: If the current width N^{(t)} is 0, the maximum defining p_0 is taken over an empty index set and is not defined. The paper explicitly uses empty-network initialization, so the algorithm as written is not well-defined at the first iteration.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a convention such as p_0 = 0 (or -\infty) when N^{(t)} = 0, so that insertion is governed only by \hat p > \alpha.
issues.overall_effect: The executable algorithm is incomplete for the stated initialization and for any iteration that prunes all nodes.
issues.title: Main algorithm undefined for empty network in Phase I
issues.why_classification: A local pseudocode convention fixes the well-definedness issue without changing the method's guarantees or architecture.
